![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/5eac1b1d21378d64b90fc2463eb7664b30224594ba5d63aa70a7c412097012a0.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $x=1+y$ and $x=1-2y+{y}^{2},$ as shown above. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(y)=1+y$ and $g(y)=1-2y+{y}^{2}.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 1+y & =1-2y+{y}^{2} \\ 3y-{y}^{2} & =0 \\ y(3-y) & =0 \\ y & =0,3\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions corresponding to our region are $y=0$ and $y=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=3.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/84e62b99598649ac48d55171b0d6bf7e5d26e38a6ad94c46ef9c89145e60e29a.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=1-2y+{y}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=1+y.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}y([1+y]-[1-2y+{y}^{2}])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}y(3y-{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}(3{y}^{2}-{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi (3{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{3}\text{d}y) \\  & =2\pi ({3\cdot \frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{3}-{\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{3}) \\  & =2\pi (3(\frac{27}{3}-0)-(\frac{81}{4}-0)) \\  & =2\pi (27-\frac{81}{4}) \\  & =\frac{27\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
